title: Hummingbird

summary.en: A real-time classroom observation and feedback tool co-designed with teachers, built around the insight that teachers operate in 2–3 second windows between student interactions: large tap-without-looking UI, arm's-length typography, and one-tap interactions, refined over five prototype iterations tested directly in classrooms.
summary.jp: 教師は生徒対応の合間、2〜3 秒しか手が空かない。その前提から逆算し、見ずに押せる大きなボタンと離れた距離でも読める文字にした。教師とのワークショップで作り、教室での試作を 5 回重ねた。

product.en: The design constraint came from classroom reality, not a feature list: teachers get 2–3 seconds between student interactions, so every UI decision — tap targets, typography size, the donut-wheel interaction — was set by that window, refined across five in-classroom prototype rounds.
product.jp: 制約は機能一覧ではなく教室の現実から来た。教師の手が空くのは 2〜3 秒。タップ範囲も文字の大きさも「ドーナツ型」の操作も、その時間から逆算して決めた。

mine: Co-designed with teachers through workshops rather than observing from behind glass
Identified the key constraint shaping the design: teachers operate in 2–3 second windows between student interactions
Prioritized larger tap-without-looking UI elements, arm's-length typography and fewer decision points (1 tap vs. 3)
Designed the 'donut-wheel' interaction for the 2–3 second window
Tested 5 prototype iterations directly in classrooms and refined based on actual mid-lesson use
team: Project Manager, Education Experts, UX Designer, UI Designer and Software Engineer — credited on the page by role title, without individual task breakdown

metrics.basis: as reported on the case-study page

label.en: prototype iterations refined through usability testing in real classrooms

narrative.problem: Teachers needed real-time student feedback, but existing tools disrupted the learning environment — the act of monitoring was breaking the thing being monitored, demanding too much attention and pulling teachers out of the flow of instruction.

_notes: Amplify-affiliated but not covered by roles.json's Amplify → ela-quests mapping, so engagement recorded as unstated rather than employee.
The 40% efficiency figure is reported on the page without a stated methodology; recorded with confidence 'stated' since the page does not itself flag it as a projection.

cardLine.en: Teachers get two or three seconds between students. The interface is built for that.
cardLine.jp: 教員が使えるのは生徒の合間の 2〜3 秒。その前提でつくった画面。
